transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling tired all the time, and I don't have any energy. It's been going on for about two months now and it's not getting any better.
Do you have any allergies, or have you ever had a bad reaction to a medicine?
Yes, codeine makes me very sick. I've never had a problem with anything else that I know of.
How much is the tiredness getting in the way of your usual daily activities?
Quite a lot, really. I used to go swimming twice a week and I've had to stop that, and I'm struggling to help my husband wash and dress in the mornings now.
What medicines do you take regularly these days, and has anything changed recently?

I take metformin 500 mg twice a day for my diabetes, levothyroxine 100 micrograms every morning for my thyroid, and omeprazole 20 mg once a day for indigestion. I also take ibuprofen 400 mg most days that I buy from the chemist for my shoulder pain. Nothing's changed recently.
Along with the tiredness, have you noticed anything else different about how you feel?

Yes, I get more short of breath than usual when I'm walking on hills, and a couple of friends have said I look pale. I sleep about seven hours but I wake up unrefreshed, and my mood feels a bit flat with all the caring.
Do you feel the tiredness in any particular part of your body, or is it more general?
It's not in any one spot, it's just a general tiredness all over. It's there all day, though it seems worse in the afternoon.
Is there anything that seems to make your tiredness better or worse?
Resting helps a little, but not for long. It's definitely worse in the afternoon, and I now need a nap most days, which is new for me.
You've mentioned your diabetes and thyroid condition — is there anything else from your past health, like other conditions, illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you'd like to add?
No, that's it really — just the diabetes, which I've had for about 12 years, and the underactive thyroid. I haven't had any operations or hospital stays.
What worries you most about how you've been feeling lately?
I'm worried I won't be able to keep looking after my husband. He has Parkinson's and I'm the one who does everything for him, so if I keep feeling like this I don't know how I'll manage.
How would you describe what the tiredness actually feels like for you?
It just feels like I've got no energy at all, like I'm running on empty. If I had to put a number on it, I'd say my energy is about a 3 out of 10.
Is there anything else you take for your health that you haven't mentioned yet?
No, nothing else. Those are the only medicines I take.
Aside from what you've already mentioned, is there anything else you've noticed that you'd like to tell me about?
No, I think I've covered everything. That's all I've noticed.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
